<!-- pr-reviewer: 1eff24249dd14825aba04999d83d5b44ed38a130 -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge.** (Reviewed at the high tier: motion toolpath planning, under the safety floor.)

**What looks good**
- The four rings arms of `plan_level` (seam-crossed, narrowed helix, wrap planner refusal, and `adaptive_passes`' own fallback) keep their exact behaviour. `rings_named` calls `plan_passes(center, p.tiling_step(), p.climb, OffsetRings)`, the same step the old inline arms used (`tiling_step()` is the load step under Adaptive), and returns `LevelPlan::rings(.., p.helix_radius)`. The note text is unchanged and the order is the same. The `what` string just moves above the seam arm, so it is now computed once.
- Nothing is lost. The planar-ladder `(Err, None) => return Err(e)` refusal is untouched, and the rest and shell single-note arms (`note_once`) are untouched.
- The guard cannot hide a level. It only adds a note, and only when `s != Adaptive` and no planner note ends with this level's `rings_tag(what)`. It does not change the passes, the strategy or the returned plan. The existing path always satisfies it, because `adaptive_passes` emits `... - Offset rings cut {what} instead` with the same `what`. So it is dead today (the PR says so) and cannot flip a verdict.
- The reader change is a test-fixture fix only. The fixture now reads just the `top - k*step` planes, which are the ladder's own levels. The 5.6 microlift plane was the phantom level the earlier version read.
- Three new pins in `hsm_fallback_tests.rs`: wrap refusal, planar refusal and seam each assert the note's tail and that rings cut the level. Plus the microlift reader pin. Provenance lines present. No snapshots, goldens, CHANGELOG, `build.rs`, scripts, dependencies or process files touched. The decision record is in `docs/decisions/`. `hsm.rs` is 339 lines.

**Local results (merged with current main, macOS)**
Trial merge was clean (main adds only `pocket3d_hsm.rs` in app and a decision file).
| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `camcraft-motion --lib` | 192 passed, 1 ignored |
| `adaptive_hsm` | 1 passed (5 ignored) |
| `adaptive_band` | 2 passed |
| `pocket3d_hsm` (motion) | 3 passed |
| `rotary_adaptive` | 3 passed |
| release `--ignored` `rotary_adaptive` | 3 passed |
| release `--ignored` `adaptive_hsm` | 5 passed |
| `clippy -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -D warnings` | clean |

App and UI suites were not run: no output or note text changed.

**Requested before merge**
None.

**Notes (not blocking)**
1. `read_levels` now drops any level off the `top - k*step` ladder. A real level the planner clamped off-ladder (a floor that is not a multiple of the stepdown) would not be read, so the "every ring level is named" assertions would not see it. Every current caller has a floor on the ladder (stepdowns 0.5, 1 and 2), so nothing is hidden today. Consider a short comment in the fixture, or an assert that the floor sits on the ladder.
2. The guard has no driving test, as the PR says. Fine for a defensive branch.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

<!-- pr-reviewer: 1eff24249dd14825aba04999d83d5b44ed38a130 -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge.** This is an independent, high-tier review. It covers a toolpath generator, so the safety floor applies. The PR was trial-merged with current `origin/main` (3e9b8ae1), and the merge was clean.

### What looks good
- **The notes are unchanged, byte for byte.** Each of the three moved arms in `plan_level` (seam crossed, narrowed helix, hard refusal on the wrap) builds the same string as before through `rings_named` + `rings_tag` (`crates/motion/src/machining3d/hsm.rs:136-176,223-234`). The rings tiling step is also the same as before: `p.tiling_step()`, the old `step`.
- **The guard cannot double-note.** `adaptive_passes`' own fallback note ends in `- Offset rings cut {what} instead` (`machining2d/pocket_hsm.rs:67-68`), which is exactly `rings_tag(&what)`. So the guard at `hsm.rs:179-182` stays quiet on every current path, and no level is named twice. It only fires when `s != Adaptive`, so a level the HSM plan did plan is never named. The trochoid door is not taken from `plan_level` (`trochoid = false`).
- **The moves are unchanged.** golden_cl passes 25/25. The bore pin prints exactly main's counts and notes (below).
- **The #983 diagnosis is right.** The level reader used to count any plane that a non-rapid descent ends on. A microlift's down ramp with a vertex on its lifted height therefore made up a "ring-cut, unnamed" level. Restricting the reader to the ladder's planes `top - k*step` (`tests/rotary_adaptive_fixture/mod.rs:171-175`) fixes that, and `a_microlift_plane_is_not_read_as_an_unnamed_ring_level` pins it.
- Three unit pins in `crates/motion` force a planner refusal (planar and developed) and a seam crossing, then check the name and the reason.
- No `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic!` outside tests. The new test file carries its provenance line. The decision file is present. No process files, build.rs, `.github`, dependencies or goldens are touched.

### Local results (Windows, merged with main)
| Run | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -p camcraft-motion --tests` (lib 192, adaptive_band 2, adaptive_hsm 1, finish3d 55, flow 13, pocket3d_hsm 3, rotary_adaptive 3, ...) | all pass |
| `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test pocket3d_hsm` | 1 passed, 1 ignored |
| release `--ignored the_users_bore_roughs_adaptive_level_by_level_and_verifies_clean --exact` | pass |
| app `golden_cl` | 25 passed |
| app `conformance` | 6 passed |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

The bore pin prints the same values as on main. Z 20 and Z 10 are each named once:
```
moves 6500 planar 6464 arcs 222 notes ["adaptive: the HSM plan for this area crosses itself at (-1.66, -2.80) - Offset rings cut the level at Z 20.000 instead", ..., "adaptive: the HSM plan for this area crosses itself at (-1.99, -0.13) - Offset rings cut the level at Z 10.000 instead", ...]
```

### Requested before merge
None.

### Notes (non-blocking)
1. **The ladder filter can miss an off-grid floor.** `cut_levels` always pushes `bottom` as the last level, even when it is off the stepdown grid (`machining2d/levels.rs:86`). The new `on_ladder` filter would drop such a floor, so a ring-cut floor could escape `assert_refusals_named`. The current fixtures have their floors on the grid, so nothing is hidden today. Consider also keeping the lowest descent plane (or the passed `floor`) in `read_levels`. This is test-only code.
2. **Interaction with #1032 (orbit seam).** The two PRs touch no common file, and a `git merge-tree` of both heads is clean. Their intent does not conflict either: this PR changes neither notes nor moves on the bore, and none of its tests rely on a bore level falling back. Either can merge first, with nothing to re-measure. If #1032 lands first, its new bore pin (empty fallback set) stays valid with this change, because the guard only adds a note when a fallback carries none.
3. **The guard is untested.** It cannot fire today, as the body says. That is fine as a defensive belt.
4. `hsm.rs` grows from 321 to 339 lines, which is still under 400.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
